thread.title: China Reportedly Inserted Spy Chips Into Servers Used By Apple, Others | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: China Reportedly Inserted Spy Chips Into Servers Used By Apple, Others | Investor's Business Daily
text:
A news report claiming that the Chinese government installed spy chips into servers purchased by Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ) and other U.S. companies has set off alarm bells about the security of the supply chain for information technology hardware in China.
X Bloomberg Businessweek reported Thursday that data center equipment run by Amazon Web Services and Apple may have been subject to surveillance from the Chinese government via a tiny microchip inserted during the equipment manufacturing process. In separate statements, Amazon and Apple strongly disputed the facts in the article, which cites current and former U.S. intelligence sources.
Bloomberg said officials discovered the security breach in 2015 and it has been subject of a top-secret investigation since then. Companies that had installed the affected servers have since pulled the gear, it said.
Almost 30 U.S. companies installed the affected hardware, supplied by Super Micro Computers, Bloomberg said. The chip, about the size of a grain of rice, was designed to bypass security protocols, relay information and even alter software systems. It even found its way into U.S. Defense Department systems, the report said.
In a press release , Super Micro also refuted the claims in the Bloomberg article.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Server Maker Delisted Super Micro reported in August 2016 that it had lost two major customers, one later identified in news reports as Apple. Concurrent with the investigation over the spy chips, Super Micro reported accounting problems related to revenue recognition.
The San Jose, Calif.-based company was delisted from the Nasdaq on Aug. 23 after missing two deadlines to file quarterly and annual reports with U.S. regulators. Super Micro now trades on the so-called Pink Sheets over-the-counter exchange.
Its shares fell 41% to 12.60 on the stock market today , CNBC reported . Earlier in the session, it dropped as much as 60% to 8.50.
Meanwhile, shares of Apple slipped 1.8% to 227.99 while Amazon lost 2.2% to 1,909.42. The stock market fell broadly on Thursday as interest rates hit multiyear highs.
The Bloomberg report is alarming because the U.S. tech industry has outsourced much of its hardware business to low-cost contract manufacturers in China and Southeast Asia.
